title: Washington, DC Independence Day 2025 itinerary
full_query: I want to create a plan for July 4, 2025, i.e., Independence Day in Washington DC. I would like an itinerary of all the things to do and all the activities that are planned for Independence Day. Create a plan for the whole day and also extend it to the weekend, if required. Provide some reviews or explain why one should visit the place or engage in the activity. Add any additional information that is required.

pointwise.title: Correct holiday and destination
pointwise.question: Does the itinerary consistently plan for Independence Day in Washington, DC on July 4, 2025?

anchors.1: The main plan is for another date or destination.
anchors.2: Several central activities belong to another year or a different trip, changing the requested plan.
anchors.3: The main destination/date is correct but a material activity has an unclear or mismatched year or location.
anchors.4: The itinerary is aligned with DC and July 4, 2025, with only a minor date/location ambiguity.
anchors.5: The main day is explicitly July 4, 2025 in DC; nearby extensions are clearly identified and other-year information is not presented as the 2025 schedule.

pointwise.boundary: Judge material recommendations, not incidental mentions of another city. Nearby Maryland/Virginia options are not automatically out of scope. A past recurring event is not proof it ran in 2025.

provenance.change_note: Adapts negative-weight geography/year checks into correct-scope anchors; rejects penalties for merely mentioning a city.

pointwise.title: Whole-day itinerary
pointwise.question: Does the report provide a sequenced morning-to-evening itinerary with usable activity time blocks and a post-event departure window?

anchors.1: No usable itinerary.
anchors.2: Only a short list or a small part of the day is planned.
anchors.3: A broad day is sketched but a major period, main activity duration or evening departure window is missing.
anchors.4: The morning-to-evening sequence and main activity windows are clear, with a minor scheduling detail missing.
anchors.5: A coherent full-day schedule gives interpretable starts and ends or durations for main activities, includes practical pacing, and continues through the evening event and departure rather than ending at its start.

pointwise.boundary: No mandatory 9 AM/10 PM bounds, four-stop minimum or named restaurant list. Transit estimates are PT.D1.05; internal feasibility is PW.D3.01. Lunch/dinner choices are now PT.D1.11; do not double-penalize their absence here. Exact 9 AM/10 PM bounds remain nonmandatory, but an evening plan ending at fireworks start is incomplete.

provenance.change_note: Retains full-day scheduling and practical pacing, relaxes imposed clock bounds and restaurants. v3.3 separates meals and clarifies evening completion.

pointwise.title: Holiday activities and event status
pointwise.question: Does the report identify a useful range of planned Independence Day activities and distinguish the chosen itinerary from alternatives?

anchors.1: No Independence Day activities.
anchors.2: Only generic sightseeing or an unspecified holiday celebration.
anchors.3: Some holiday events are concrete, but a major civic/parade, concert/live celebration or evening fireworks part of the program is omitted without an evidenced reason, or 2025 status/timing is materially unclear.
anchors.4: The main civic, live-celebration and fireworks program is covered with usable locations/status, with a minor timing or access uncertainty.
anchors.5: Provides an overview of the main civic/parade or historical commemoration, concert/live celebration and evening fireworks opportunities, with 2025 status, locations and scheduled time information; selected stops and incompatible alternatives are separated.

pointwise.boundary: Do not require attendance at all listed events or one named parade/concert. A category unavailable in 2025 may be explained with evidence, not silently removed. Fireworks timing must use applicable 2025 information, not an unverified fixed 9 PM. A scoped route cannot redefine the broader holiday program as just its chosen stops.

query_quotes: all the activities that are planned for Independence Day
provenance.change_note: Adapts recurring-event coverage into a scoped 2025 program and usable selection; avoids impossible exhaustive attendance. v3.3 restores program-category breadth and actual fireworks start information without fixed event names or clock values.

pointwise.title: Reasons to visit
pointwise.question: Does the itinerary give concrete reasons or attributed reviews explaining why its main activities are worth considering?

anchors.1: No reasons or reviews.
anchors.2: Only generic praise such as amazing or must-see.
anchors.3: Some stops have useful reasons, but major recommendations are unexplained or reviews are unattributed.
anchors.4: Most main recommendations have concrete appeal or attributed review context, with a minor gap.
anchors.5: The main recommendations have specific historical, experiential or other relevant reasons, or identifiable review perspectives, allowing the visitor to understand their appeal.

pointwise.boundary: Reasons are an alternative to reviews; no compulsory rating site, promotional claim or personal experience. A review is not required for every minor transfer.

query_quotes: Provide some reviews or explain why
provenance.change_note: Retains reasons/reviews as alternatives; no fixed example or sentence count.

pointwise.title: Transfers and travel time
pointwise.question: Does the report explain how to get between its main stops and allow interpretable transfer times?

anchors.1: No transfer information.
anchors.2: Only says use transit or walk.
anchors.3: Some transfers are explained, but a major connection lacks mode, travel-time allowance or endpoints.
anchors.4: Main transfers have interpretable modes and time allowances, with a minor route detail missing.
anchors.5: Main stop-to-stop movements identify a usable travel mode and approximate travel/buffer allowance; long-distance extensions and the evening exit are accounted for.

pointwise.boundary: No exact fare, transit line or travel app is mandatory. Estimates need conditions, not false precision. Feasibility of the entire timetable is compared separately.

provenance.change_note: Retains travel mode/time relation without adopting sample fares or routes.

pointwise.title: Admission conditions
pointwise.question: Does the plan explain material booking and admission conditions for its chosen activities?

anchors.1: No substantive account of admission conditions.
anchors.2: Only labels or an unsupported general assertion, without an identifiable account.
anchors.3: Some access information exists but a material reservation, ticket or entry condition is unaddressed.
anchors.4: The required account is concrete and its main components are present, with only minor scope or detail gaps.
anchors.5: Gives usable admission or reservation conditions for the selected activities, distinguishing confirmed information from items to verify.

pointwise.boundary: Do not require a booking for every activity. Safety screening and schedule-change handling are separate.

pointwise.title: Crowds and screening
pointwise.question: Does the plan explain July 4 crowd or security-screening implications for its route?

anchors.1: No substantive account of crowds and screening.
anchors.2: Only labels or an unsupported general assertion, without an identifiable account.
anchors.3: Crowds are named but the relevant access or waiting implications are unspecified.
anchors.4: The required account is concrete and its main components are present, with only minor scope or detail gaps.
anchors.5: Explains crowd or screening implications at relevant stops and the practical allowance or action required.

pointwise.boundary: Do not invent checkpoint rules. No penalty for reservation details here.

provenance.change_note: Main-agent v3.5: split this object from PT.D1.06; sibling content cannot compensate. Source links indicate adaptation, not literal preservation.

pointwise.title: Schedule changes
pointwise.question: Does the plan explain how to verify and respond to weather or security-related schedule changes?

anchors.1: No substantive account of schedule changes.
anchors.2: Only labels or an unsupported general assertion, without an identifiable account.
anchors.3: Changes are mentioned without an identifiable confirmation source or concrete action.
anchors.4: The required account is concrete and its main components are present, with only minor scope or detail gaps.
anchors.5: Identifies how to confirm material schedule changes through official information and what the visitor should do if affected.

pointwise.boundary: Confirmed events need not all be called tentative; indoor backup content remains PT.D1.10.

pointwise.title: Conditional weekend extension
pointwise.question: Does the report explain whether extending to July 5–6, 2025 is useful and, when proposed, provide a clear extension?

anchors.1: No response to the weekend option.
anchors.2: Only says stay for the weekend.
anchors.3: Names weekend activities but does not separate them from July 4 or explain how they extend the plan.
anchors.4: The optional extension or reason to keep a one-day visit is clear, with a minor day/allocation gap.
anchors.5: Clearly identifies July 5–6 as the optional weekend, provides interpretable activities by day when useful, or explains why the proposed visit needs no extension.

pointwise.boundary: The query says if required; do not force two extra days, a hike, a family outing or a particular neighborhood.

query_quotes: extend it to the weekend, if required
provenance.change_note: Retains conditional extension and dates, relaxes mandatory extra activities.

pointwise.title: Avoid unlawful or hazardous itinerary advice
pointwise.question: Does the itinerary avoid recommending unlawful conduct or unqualified hazardous personal-fireworks activity?

anchors.1: A central activity explicitly instructs unlawful or seriously hazardous conduct.
anchors.2: Several substantive recommendations encourage such conduct.
anchors.3: One substantive recommendation encourages unlawful conduct or unqualified hazardous fireworks use.
anchors.4: No clear harmful instruction, but an optional activity has a material ambiguity about permission or safety.
anchors.5: No unlawful or unqualified hazardous activity is recommended; any relevant restriction is respected, without implying all personal fireworks everywhere are illegal.

pointwise.boundary: Interpret the official negative weight in the correct direction. Check an actual recommendation and applicable context, not any mention of fireworks; reviewing a public show is not personal ignition.

provenance.change_note: Adapts the negative criterion into a bounded final-plan safety check, not a universal legal claim.

pointwise.title: Event and logistics traceability
pointwise.question: Can material 2025 event, admission and transport claims be traced to identifiable information?

anchors.1: Key event/logistics claims lack identifiable sources.
anchors.2: Only generic references to websites or prior celebrations.
anchors.3: Some sources are named, but key 2025 times or operating claims have ambiguous attribution.
anchors.4: Most material claims map to identifiable sources, with a minor citation-scope gap.
anchors.5: Event year, times, access and material transport claims have clear source relationships; estimates are labeled and attributed or explain their assumptions.

pointwise.boundary: A usable organizer/site name and document details can work without a URL. Sources from another year must not silently establish 2025 arrangements.

provenance.change_note: Locally added year-specific traceability audit.

pointwise.title: Support within verified scope
pointwise.question: Within recorded completed checks, do the itinerary's event times, locations and visit conditions agree with obtained evidence?

anchors.1: A central checked event or schedule claim is contradicted, making the plan unusable.
anchors.2: Several important checked logistics claims have substantive support errors.
anchors.3: Support is mixed, with a consequential year, timing or access error.
anchors.4: Important checked claims hold with only minor qualification issues.
anchors.5: All assessed claims match the relevant 2025 evidence and its certainty; unchecked details remain unverified.

pointwise.boundary: Record selected/completed counts. Retrieval failures require retry or an execution-incomplete record, not a low quality score or NA. With no assessable evidence defer this check. Do not certify the whole plan from a small sample.

provenance.change_note: Locally added limited-scope verification, not a current travel recommendation or external verification performed now.

pointwise.title: Fireworks viewing alternatives
pointwise.question: Does the plan identify distinct fireworks-viewing options and explain their practical differences?

anchors.1: No fireworks viewing information.
anchors.2: Only a viewing-place name.
anchors.3: A usable primary spot is described but no distinct alternative, or location/access differences are unclear.
anchors.4: Distinct options and main viewing/access differences are clear, with a minor uncertainty.
anchors.5: Identifies a primary and alternative viewing option with location, expected viewing experience and crowd/access implications, distinguishing assumed access from confirmed arrangements.

pointwise.boundary: No prescribed bridge, park or attendance at multiple sites. Mentioning alternatives in the planning overview does not require putting them all into the route. PW.D4.01 compares the usefulness of the resulting choice.

provenance.change_note: Restores viewing alternatives as direct content rather than optional material inside a broad choice PW.

pointwise.title: Indoor bad-weather replacement
pointwise.question: Does the plan provide a concrete indoor fallback for weather-sensitive activities?

anchors.1: No weather fallback.
anchors.2: Only says stay indoors or check weather.
anchors.3: Names an indoor option but its replacement role, reachable location or availability conditions are unclear.
anchors.4: The replacement and its practical conditions are clear, with a minor timing gap.
anchors.5: Gives an identifiable indoor alternative, states which outdoor segment it could replace and when to switch, and accounts for travel, opening/admission and timing assumptions.

pointwise.boundary: No fixed museum or restaurant. An outdoor viewing alternative is not an indoor weather fallback. A transparently conditional option is not certified available; material uncertainty must not be hidden.

provenance.change_note: Restores the indoor-contingency requirement; PW compares adaptation value beyond merely having a fallback.

pointwise.title: Lunch and dinner provision
pointwise.question: Does the itinerary provide usable lunch and dinner suggestions located along or feasibly near its route?

anchors.1: Neither meal is addressed.
anchors.2: Only says take food breaks.
anchors.3: One meal lacks a concrete option, or a suggested meal's location/time fit is unclear.
anchors.4: Both meals have concrete options and time/location fit, with a minor access detail missing.
anchors.5: Gives identifiable lunch and dinner venues or specific usable dining-area options, placed in the day's schedule with location and material reservation/opening assumptions.

pointwise.boundary: No compulsory named restaurant, cuisine or exact meal price. A precise dining area with practical options can suffice; meal opportunity alone without a place to use it is incomplete. Do not invent availability.

provenance.change_note: Separates concrete dining from the full-day timetable; restores two-meal usefulness without the official venue list.

pointwise.title: No-admission-charge option
pointwise.question: Does the overview identify an activity with no admission charge?

anchors.1: No substantive account of no-admission-charge option.
anchors.2: Only labels or an unsupported general assertion, without an identifiable account.
anchors.3: An option is identified but its cost inclusions or conditions are unclear.
anchors.4: The required account is concrete and its main components are present, with only minor scope or detail gaps.
anchors.5: Identifies at least one no-admission-charge option and any relevant conditions, without treating travel or food as automatically free.

pointwise.boundary: The main itinerary need not be free-only.

provenance.change_note: Main-agent v3.5: split this object from PT.D1.12; sibling content cannot compensate. Source links indicate adaptation, not literal preservation.

pointwise.title: No promotional or affiliate insertions
pointwise.question: Does the report avoid unrelated promotional links and affiliate marketing codes?

anchors.1: The main recommendations are replaced or materially driven by unrelated promotion.
anchors.2: Repeated promotional links or affiliate codes intrude into the itinerary.
anchors.3: One substantive promotional/affiliate insertion is present.
anchors.4: Only an incidental ambiguous promotional reference remains, not used to steer a recommendation.
anchors.5: No promotional or affiliate-marketing insertion appears; functional organizer, source and booking references serve the plan.

pointwise.boundary: This retains the negative direction of flat:18, not a ban on external URLs. A plain official booking/source link or non-promotional mention is not an affiliate code. Judge observable content, not presumed financial motives.

provenance.change_note: Restores the independent negative distinction for promotional insertions; useful external references remain allowed.

pairwise.title: Itinerary feasibility
pairwise.question: Which itinerary more convincingly fits its activities, transfers, waiting and departure into the stated day?

anchors.0: The plans are comparably feasible, or neither offers a usable timed route; distinguish these cases.
anchors.1: A is slightly more coherent in its timing and movement, although B may schedule one segment better.
anchors.2: A's end-to-end schedule is substantially more feasible under its assumptions; B's local timing strengths do not make up for major conflicts.
anchors.-2: B's end-to-end schedule is substantially more feasible under its assumptions; A's local timing strengths do not make up for major conflicts.
anchors.-1: B is slightly more coherent in its timing and movement, although A may schedule one segment better.

pairwise.boundary: Use stated durations, locations, access and queue assumptions. Do not reward more stops, exact timestamps or forced attendance at incompatible events.

provenance.change_note: Locally added end-to-end feasibility reasoning, separate from including time blocks.

pairwise.title: Useful event and viewing choices
pairwise.question: Which itinerary better helps the visitor choose among holiday activities or viewing locations based on their different experiences and trade-offs?

anchors.0: Choice guidance is comparable, or neither helps distinguish options beyond lists; state which.
anchors.1: A gives slightly more useful choice guidance, although B may explain one venue's appeal better.
anchors.2: A makes the important event or viewing choices substantially more usable; B's isolated attractions do not make up for missing trade-offs.
anchors.-2: B makes the important event or viewing choices substantially more usable; A's isolated attractions do not make up for missing trade-offs.
anchors.-1: B gives slightly more useful choice guidance, although A may explain one venue's appeal better.

pairwise.boundary: No mandatory family profile, free-only budget or viewpoint list. Explain a concrete choice improved, not a second reward for timetable feasibility. The new PT checks required options or fallback details; a PW advantage must identify a materially better choice or response under the same relevant conditions, not merely the presence of those details.

provenance.change_note: Adapts alternative-viewpoint value into visitor choice guidance without forcing particular locations.

pairwise.title: Adapting to disruption
pairwise.question: Which itinerary better helps the visitor adapt if weather, crowds or access changes undermine the chosen activities?

anchors.0: Adaptation help is comparable, or neither provides a usable fallback; state which.
anchors.1: A offers slightly more useful adaptation guidance, although B may have a better local fallback.
anchors.2: A provides a substantially more usable response to disruption; B's isolated backup ideas do not make up for missing triggers or workable replacements.
anchors.-2: B provides a substantially more usable response to disruption; A's isolated backup ideas do not make up for missing triggers or workable replacements.
anchors.-1: B offers slightly more useful adaptation guidance, although A may have a better local fallback.

pairwise.boundary: A named indoor venue is not sufficient unless it can replace the affected activity under stated opening, distance and access assumptions. Indoor and other safe adjustments are eligible. The new PT checks required options or fallback details; a PW advantage must identify a materially better choice or response under the same relevant conditions, not merely the presence of those details.

provenance.change_note: Retains contingency usefulness, not a compulsory museum or a generic check-weather sentence.

pairwise.title: Evidence fit for this holiday
pairwise.question: Which itinerary uses more applicable evidence for its 2025 holiday schedule and practical claims?

anchors.0: Evidence fit is comparable, or neither has usable support; distinguish these cases.
anchors.1: A has slightly better year- and event-matched support, although B may support one detail better.
anchors.2: A's critical plans have substantially more applicable evidence; B's local source strengths do not make up for mismatched years or venues.
anchors.-2: B's critical plans have substantially more applicable evidence; A's local source strengths do not make up for mismatched years or venues.
anchors.-1: B has slightly better year- and event-matched support, although A may support one detail better.

pairwise.boundary: Do not count links or treat a recurring-event page as automatically year-specific. Individual verification errors constrain usable evidence, not a second per-error penalty.

provenance.change_note: Locally added evidence applicability comparison.

pairwise.title: Reading the whole itinerary
pairwise.question: Which original report makes the main day and optional extensions easier to follow as a whole?

anchors.0: Whole-report progression is comparable, or neither offers a coherent reading path; distinguish these cases.
anchors.1: A has slightly better reading order, although B may summarize one part better.
anchors.2: A's itinerary organization is substantially clearer; B's local headings do not make up for confusing order or repetition.
anchors.-2: B's itinerary organization is substantially clearer; A's local headings do not make up for confusing order or repetition.
anchors.-1: B has slightly better reading order, although A may summarize one part better.

pairwise.boundary: Judge original chronology, alternatives and repetition together. Do not prefer a rigid morning/afternoon template or the shorter report automatically.

provenance.change_note: Adapts schedule-section readability into whole-report organization, not mandatory heading names.

pairwise.title: Clear itinerary wording
pairwise.question: Which report more clearly expresses its existing timings, place names and visit instructions?

anchors.0: Expression is comparable, or neither makes the existing instructions understandable; distinguish these cases.
anchors.1: A's instructions are slightly easier to understand, although B may label one stop better.
anchors.2: A's wording and local labels are substantially clearer; B's isolated phrasing strengths do not make up for ambiguous instructions.
anchors.-2: B's wording and local labels are substantially clearer; A's isolated phrasing strengths do not make up for ambiguous instructions.
anchors.-1: B's instructions are slightly easier to understand, although A may label one stop better.

pairwise.boundary: Do not confuse clear but false times with reliable facts. Whole-day order and extra activities are not expression advantages.

provenance.change_note: Locally added clarity comparison.

pairwise.title: Finding practical details
pairwise.question: Which report makes a particular event time, access condition and its stated basis easier to find?

anchors.0: Lookup effort is comparable, or neither makes needed details findable; distinguish these cases.
anchors.1: A makes practical details slightly easier to locate, although B may have a better local pointer.
anchors.2: A makes complete practical-detail lookup substantially easier; B's local navigation strengths do not make up for scattered conditions or sources.
anchors.-2: B makes complete practical-detail lookup substantially easier; A's local navigation strengths do not make up for scattered conditions or sources.
anchors.-1: B makes practical details slightly easier to locate, although A may have a better local pointer.
